title: Site and speed
hired_for: So a shopper on a phone sees the product and can tap buy before they lose patience, which shows up as lower bounce, higher mobile conversion and more revenue.

jobs.job: Make the main product image show fast on phones, starting with the pages ads land on
jobs.why: If the product does not appear in about 2.5 seconds, many phone shoppers leave before they see it. On ad landing pages, every one of those exits is a paid click thrown away.

watch.metric: largest contentful paint (time until the main image or text shows), mobile, 75th percentile, 28 days, top ad landing page and top product page

drives.metric: bounce rate from paid mobile traffic on those pages, 28 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the top product page shows its main image at 4.1 s and paid mobile bounce is 64%. After: 2.3 s; bounce 55% once 28 days of field data land.
jobs.who_today: developer or speed agency, once a year

jobs.job: Shrink heavy images without making them look worse
jobs.why: Images are most of the weight on most store pages. Camera size photos on a phone mean a long wait for a picture the shopper sees at 400 pixels wide.

watch.metric: image weight on the 5 key templates, lab test, latest run

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the product page loads 3,800 KB of images, one hero at 1,900 KB. After: 900 KB with no visible loss; lab paint time down 1.2 s the same day.

jobs.job: Catch a slowdown the day an app or theme change causes it
jobs.why: A new app can add a second to every page without anyone noticing. Sales slip for weeks while the team looks at the ads.

watch.metric: lab load time and page weight against the budget for each page type, checked after every change

jobs.now_after: Example: Now a reviews app added 600 KB and 0.9 s last month and no one saw it for 5 weeks. After: flagged the day it was installed, with the app named.

jobs.job: Put a dollar figure on slowness so I know if it is worth fixing
jobs.why: Speed work competes with ads and new products for money. A number in the store's own dollars, from its own conversion rate and traffic, decides if it goes first.

watch.metric: mobile conversion rate by page speed band (fast, medium, slow sessions), 30 days
watch.source: GA4 joined to PageSpeed field data

jobs.now_after: Example: Now no one knows. After: slow product page sessions convert at 1.0% against 1.6% for fast ones, about $9,000 a month at current traffic.
jobs.who_today: nobody, or a vendor's generic number

jobs.job: Remove or delay scripts that block the page and earn nothing
jobs.why: Chat, review, popup and tracking scripts often load before the product. Some are unused. Each one makes the shopper wait longer to see what they came for.

watch.metric: outside script weight and count on the 5 key templates, lab test
watch.source: PageSpeed Insights lab data and request list

drives.metric: largest contentful paint and interaction delay, mobile

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 23 outside scripts, 1,100 KB, 6 from apps no one uses. After: 12 scripts, 480 KB; 4 delayed until the first tap.

jobs.job: Test the pages ads land on inside the Instagram and Facebook in-app browser
jobs.why: Ad clicks open inside the app's own browser, which is often slower than Safari or Chrome. A page that is fast on a laptop can crawl there.

watch.metric: bounce rate from Meta paid mobile traffic, 7 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now Meta mobile bounce is 68% against 49% from Google. After: in-app issues fixed; Meta mobile bounce 57%.

jobs.job: Stop videos, sliders and animations from slowing the first screen
jobs.why: An auto playing hero video or a 5 slide carousel can double the weight of the first screen. A single strong image usually sells as well and loads far faster.

watch.metric: first screen media weight on home and product pages, lab test

drives.metric: bounce rate on those pages, mobile, 28 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the home page hero is a 6 MB video. After: a 180 KB image with a tap to play video lower down; bounce down 6 points.

jobs.job: Make add to cart, size picks and filters respond at once
jobs.why: When a tap freezes the page for half a second, shoppers tap again, pick the wrong size or give up. It feels broken even when it is not.

watch.metric: interaction to next paint (delay after a tap), mobile, 75th percentile, 28 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the size picker freezes for 480 ms. After: 170 ms; mobile add to cart up from 6.0% to 6.6%.

jobs.job: Tell me when to stop chasing the speed score
jobs.why: Once pages pass Google's marks, more speed work pays less. Stripping a feature that sells just to win points loses money.

watch.metric: key page groups passing Core Web Vitals (main image by 2.5 s, tap delay under 200 ms, little jumping), share
watch.source: Search Console Core Web Vitals report

drives.metric: mobile conversion rate held or rising

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the agency wants $4,000 to move a score from 78 to 95 on pages that already pass. After: the spend moves to the 2 page groups that fail.
jobs.who_today: agency, which often wants to keep going

jobs.job: Keep ad tracking working after every speed change
jobs.why: Delaying or moving scripts can stop the Meta pixel or GA4 from counting purchases. Ads then learn from bad data and cost more.

watch.metric: purchases counted by Meta against Shopify orders, 7 days
watch.source: Meta Events Manager and Shopify orders

jobs.now_after: Example: Now after a script delay, Meta counts 61% of orders, down from 88%. After: back to 88% within 1 day, with events checked after every change.

jobs.job: Hand the developer a brief with a pass mark and a way back
jobs.why: 'Make the site faster' gets billed hours and vague results. A brief that names the change, the target number and how to undo it gets done right the first time.

watch.metric: fixes shipped that hit their pass mark on the first try, share
watch.source: brand brain fix log with PageSpeed before and after runs

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 2 of 5 speed jobs met their goal and 1 broke the cart. After: 5 of 5 with a named target and a tested rollback.
jobs.who_today: agency or developer, often with no written target

jobs.job: Stop the page jumping while it loads so shoppers do not tap the wrong thing
jobs.why: When a banner or review stars load late and push the page down, shoppers tap the wrong button or lose their place. It feels careless.

watch.metric: cumulative layout shift (how much the page jumps), mobile, 75th percentile, 28 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the product page jumps at 0.28 when the review widget loads. After: space reserved; 0.05.

jobs.job: Speed up the cart and checkout steps
jobs.why: Shoppers who reach the cart are close to buying. A slow cart drawer or shipping calculator loses them at the finish line.

watch.metric: cart to checkout rate and checkout abandonment, mobile, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the cart drawer takes 1.4 s to open on a phone. After: 0.3 s; cart to checkout up 3 points.

jobs.job: Get the site ready to stay fast on the biggest sale days
jobs.why: Traffic can jump 5 to 10 times on Black Friday. Pages that are fine on a normal day can slow down or fail when the money is biggest.

watch.metric: server response time and checkout completion during peak hours against a normal day

jobs.now_after: Example: Now last year's peak day server response doubled for 3 hours. After: a load test, a change freeze and a fallback plan in place 3 weeks before.

jobs.job: Prove each fix worked with before and after numbers
jobs.why: Without a measured before and after, no one knows which change helped. The team keeps paying for fixes that did nothing.

watch.metric: fixes with an averaged before and after lab run on file, share
watch.source: brand brain fix log and PageSpeed Insights

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 0 of the last 8 fixes have a before number. After: 8 of 8, each with 3 averaged runs before and after.

jobs.job: Make sure caching and the delivery network actually work
jobs.why: When pages and files are not cached near the shopper, every visit waits on the main server. Repeat visitors should get a near instant page.

watch.metric: server response time (time to first byte), mobile, 28 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now server response is 1,300 ms for shoppers outside the US. After: 400 ms with files served close to them.

jobs.job: Make fonts load without hiding the words
jobs.why: Custom fonts can keep text blank for a second or more. Shoppers see an empty page with a picture and no price.

watch.metric: font weight and time until first text shows, mobile, lab test

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 9 font files, 420 KB, text blank for 1.1 s. After: 3 files, 90 KB, text shows at once.

jobs.job: Set a speed budget per page type and hold to it
jobs.why: Pages get heavier one app and one image at a time. A written limit per page type makes every addition earn its place.

watch.metric: key pages over their weight or script budget, count, monthly

jobs.now_after: Example: Now no budget, and 4 of 5 key pages grew over 20% in 6 months. After: 0 pages over budget at each monthly check.

jobs.job: Check a new app or landing page for speed before it goes live
jobs.why: Page builder pages and new apps are often heavy. Running ads to a slow new page wastes the first weeks of spend.

watch.metric: new pages and apps that pass the speed budget before launch, share

drives.metric: bounce rate on new landing pages, first 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the last 3 campaign pages launched at twice the budget. After: each tested first; 3 of 3 within budget at launch.

jobs.job: Take a speed baseline of the key pages before touching anything
jobs.why: Without a dated starting point, no one can prove a fix helped or spot a later slowdown. It takes an afternoon.

watch.metric: key pages with a dated speed check in the last 30 days, share

jobs.now_after: Example: Now no page has a dated check. After: 6 key pages checked with 3 runs each, dated and saved.

jobs.job: Clear out broken links, redirect chains and missing files that waste load time
jobs.why: Each broken file or chain of redirects adds a wait and can break a feature. They pile up after product and theme changes.

watch.metric: redirect chains and failed file requests on key pages, count
watch.source: PageSpeed Insights request list and Search Console

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 9 failed requests and 4 redirect chains on the product page. After: 0 and 0.

jobs.job: Fix speed on every page type, not just the home page
jobs.why: Most sales happen on product and collection pages, yet the home page gets the attention. Slow collection pages lose shoppers before they find a product.

watch.metric: page groups passing Core Web Vitals, by template, share
watch.source: Search Console Core Web Vitals report

jobs.now_after: Example: Now home passes and collection and product pages fail. After: all 4 page groups pass.

jobs.job: Keep the site fast for shoppers in every country we sell to
jobs.why: A page that is fast in New York can be slow in Sydney or Mumbai. Slow pages abroad look like weak demand when the real cause is speed.

watch.metric: bounce rate by country, mobile, 30 days (proxy for speed by country)

drives.metric: revenue from countries outside the home market

jobs.now_after: Example: Now Canada bounces at 66% against 51% in the US. After: files served close to Canadian shoppers; 55%.

jobs.job: Speed up the account and reorder pages for repeat buyers
jobs.why: Repeat buyers often go straight to their account to reorder. A slow login or order history page adds friction to the easiest sale.

watch.metric: lab load time of account and order history pages, mobile

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the order history page takes 5.2 s. After: 2.4 s.

jobs.job: Speed up our own code on a custom or headless storefront
jobs.why: On a custom build, much of the slowness is in the brand's own code, not the platform. Only the team can fix it, and only if they know where it is.

watch.metric: main thread blocking time on key pages, mobile, lab test

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 1,900 ms of blocking time on the product page. After: 600 ms after splitting the code by page.
